profile.core:
Professor Andy Miah is an internationally recognised interdisciplinary research leader with 18 years of Professorial experience spanning Arts & Humanities, Science & Engineering, and Health Sciences. His work examines the ethics of emerging technologies — from AI and biotechnology to immersive media, esports, and digital health — always with a commitment to societal impact and creative practice.

He is Chair in Science Communication & Future Media at the University of Salford, where he founded and directs The Science Communication Space, a cross-university platform integrating research, creative practice, and public engagement. He is Principal Investigator on a £4.5 million Innovate UK Accelerator mobilising over 250 Greater Manchester businesses into a CreaTech innovation ecosystem, and has served for six years on the Agora Committee of the Swiss National Science Foundation, overseeing approximately £18 million in interdisciplinary public engagement funding.

Andy has published over 250 works including 10 books, among them Sport 2.0 (MIT Press, 2017) and Genetically Modified Athletes (Routledge, 2004), with a forthcoming monograph under review at Oxford University Press. He has given over 450 invited talks in more than 50 countries, received the Josh Award for Science Communication from the Science and Industry Museum, Manchester, and is a member of the DCMS College of Experts. He is a Board Member of the British Esports Federation, Commission Member of the Global Esports Federation, and Marketing Manchester Ambassador.

variants.drones:
Professor Andy Miah is one of the UK's leading authorities on drone technology, ethics, and creative practice. His book Drones: The Brilliant, the Bad, and the Beautiful (Emerald Publishing, 2020) is a foundational text examining the cultural, ethical, and creative dimensions of autonomous flying machines — from environmental research and journalism to art, performance, and civic governance.

He founded and convened the Salford Drones Research Group (2015–17) and led Project Daedalus — a NESTA, AHRC, and Arts Council England-funded collaboration (£125,000) with Abandon Normal Devices and Marshmallow Laser Feast exploring the creative potential of quadcopter technology. He has presented on drones at Google SciFoo (Palo Alto, 2015), the British Science Festival, Cheltenham Science Festival, the British Film Institute, AND festival (Grizedale Forest), York Festival of Ideas, and the UAVs in Environmental Research conference at Liverpool John Moores University. He has given evidence on drone regulation to the House of Lords and appeared on BBC, Sky News, and The Conversation.

His research treats drones not merely as technology but as cultural and ethical objects — examining their role in art, journalism, environmental monitoring, public performance, and the governance of public space. He connects this work to broader questions of AI ethics, autonomous systems, and the future of civic life.
variants.esports:
Professor Andy Miah is one of the UK's foremost academic authorities on esports, digital sport, and competitive gaming. He has been active in the sector for over a decade as a researcher, governance board member, keynote speaker, and industry adviser — combining scholarly rigour with sustained practical engagement across the full breadth of the field.

He organised the first dedicated esports research conference at a UK university (Salford, 2016), has served as Board Member of the British Esports Federation since 2019, Commission Member of the Global Esports Federation since 2020, and Commission Chair of the World Technology Games since 2025. His published work includes The Esports Question for the Olympic Movement (Journal of Olympic Studies, 2021), Esport in the Olympic and Paralympic Games (Routledge, 2020), and Sport 2.0 (MIT Press, 2017). His £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator at MediaCity included a dedicated gametech and esports R&D strand connecting academic research with industry development across Greater Manchester.

He has keynoted at the Global Esports Executive Summit (Busan, 2017), ESIC Global Esports Summits (London, 2022 and 2023), the UN ITU AI for Good programme on esports and safe digital spaces (2021), Peace and Sport International Forum (Monaco, 2019), and the Esports in Education Summit at BETT (2022, 2026).
variants.olympic-games:
Professor Andy Miah is an internationally recognised authority on the Olympic Games, sport governance, and the intersection of sport, media, and technology. He co-founded Culture @ the Olympics in 2001 — one of the first digital platforms dedicated to the cultural dimensions of the Olympic movement — and has conducted fieldwork at every Summer and Winter Games from Sydney 2000 to Milan Cortina 2026.

His books include The Olympics: The Basics (Routledge, 2012, with Beatriz Garcia) and Sport 2.0 (MIT Press, 2017), which examines the digital transformation of the Games including esports, fan engagement, and media innovation. He has published on non-accredited media at the Olympics, social media and the Games, the ethics of human enhancement in sport, and the future of esports in the Olympic programme. He mentored the IOC Young Reporters Programme (Nanjing, 2014), keynoted at the International Olympic Academy, Olympism in Action Forum (Buenos Aires, 2018), and has been funded by The British Academy (x2) and Carnegie Trust (x2) for Olympic fieldwork.

He has been a regular Olympic media commentator for BBC, The Guardian, CNN, and international outlets from Sydney 2000 through Paris 2024, and writes regularly for Culture @ the Olympics, the longest-running academic journal on the cultural dimensions of the Games.
variants.bioethics-enhancement:
Professor Andy Miah is a foundational figure in the bioethics of human enhancement, gene doping, and posthumanism, whose work has shaped academic, policy, and public debate on the ethical frontiers of biotechnology for over two decades.

His book Genetically Modified Athletes (Routledge, 2004) remains a defining text in the field and has been widely cited in policy, sport governance, and philosophical literature. This was followed by The Medicalization of Cyberspace (Routledge, 2008, with Emma Rich), examining digital health and body governance, and chapters in over 30 edited collections on posthumanism, transhumanism, genetic selection, and enhancement ethics. He has provided evidence to the UK House of Commons Science and Technology Committee, the European Parliament's STOA unit, and the World Anti-Doping Agency, and has keynoted at Harvard Law School, Oxford University, the Royal Institution of Great Britain, the Hastings Center, the European Parliament, and Yale University.

He holds an MPhil in Medical Law and Ethics from the University of Glasgow and was an International Visiting Scholar at The Hastings Center for Bioethics, New York. He is a regular broadcast commentator on biotechnology and human enhancement for BBC, The Guardian, Wired, and Washington Post.
variants.ai-ethics:
Professor Andy Miah is a leading voice on AI ethics and emerging technologies, whose work bridges philosophy, policy, and creative practice to address the ethical and societal implications of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and digital futures.

He serves as a member of the UK Government's DCMS College of Experts, was Ethics Lead for the Greater Manchester AI Foundry (2020–2023), and sits on the Oversight Committee for the PROBABLE Futures project (£3.4m) on probabilistic AI in law enforcement. He chairs the Metaverse Special Interest Group at the University of Salford, led Task and Finish Groups on AI Research Policy and AI Teaching & Learning Strategy, and advises the World Technology Group. He has presented on AI ethics at the Government Office for Science, South by Southwest, the UN ITU AI for Good programme, Edinburgh Science Festival, and the European Parliament.

His published work spans AI ethics, posthumanism, nanotechnology, autonomous systems, and digital futures — including over 250 publications and 10 books, with a forthcoming monograph under review at Oxford University Press. He is a regular media commentator on AI for BBC, Sky News, CNN, and The Conversation.
variants.science-communication:
Professor Andy Miah is an award-winning science communicator and public intellectual whose career has been defined by making complex ideas in ethics, technology, and society accessible to diverse audiences. He is Director of The Science Communication Space at the University of Salford and has given over 450 invited talks in more than 50 countries.

He leads the University's decade-long partnership with Manchester Science Festival and the FameLab North West Regional Hub, and has co-led over 100 art-science collaborations at Cheltenham Science Festival, New Scientist Live, Edinburgh Science Festival, Blue Dot, and the British Science Festival. For over six years he served on the Agora Committee of the Swiss National Science Foundation, overseeing approximately £18m in science communication and public engagement funding across 200+ projects. He received the Josh Award for Science Communication from the Science and Industry Museum, Manchester (2015).

He is a regular BBC, Sky News, and CNN broadcast contributor, a columnist for The Conversation, and most recently appeared in Future Tense (Audible, 2025, with Richard Ayoade and Warwick Davis). His book The Science Communication Imperative is under review at Oxford University Press.
variants.digital-health:
Professor Andy Miah is a leading researcher in digital health technologies, examining how wearable devices, mobile health platforms, immersive media, and AI-driven systems are transforming healthcare, wellbeing, and the governance of bodies and health data.

His co-authored book The Medicalization of Cyberspace (Routledge, 2008, with Emma Rich) was among the first sustained academic analyses of digital health as a cultural phenomenon. His Wellcome Trust-funded research (£130,000, with the Universities of Bath and Canberra) examined digital health technologies and young people, and his peer-reviewed articles in Health Sociology Review, Sociology of Health and Illness, and Societies examine equity, surveillance, and the politics of health data. He has keynoted at the Digital Health Generation events at the Houses of Parliament (2018) and Milton Keynes (2018), the Healthy City Design Conference (2025), and has written for The Conversation on AI and the NHS, mental healthcare in gaming environments, and the ethics of wearable technology.

His research connects digital health to broader questions of social responsibility, data ethics, and inclusive design — increasingly through the lens of AI, immersive technology, and VR interfaces for clinical practice.
variants.metaverse:
Professor Andy Miah is a leading academic voice on the metaverse, virtual reality, and the ethical, social, and cultural implications of immersive digital environments. He chairs the Metaverse Special Interest Group at the University of Salford, founded in 2021, and his forthcoming book Demystifying the Metaverse (Emerald Publishing) provides a comprehensive philosophical, social, and cultural analysis of this emerging domain.

His research on the metaverse spans XR design ethics, virtual sport, immersive science communication, phygital futures, and the governance of digital spaces. He led a £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator at MediaCity (2023–26) encompassing metaverse applications, virtual production, and immersive technologies across 250+ Greater Manchester businesses. He has keynoted on the metaverse at South by Southwest (Texas, 2023), the Government Office for Science (Manchester, 2023), Luxembourg National Science Foundation (2023), and the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants national conference (2023).

His published work includes The Moral Metaverse: Establishing an Ethical Foundation for XR Design (Routledge, 2023) and the chapter Virtual Reality and Sports (Springer, 2020/2023, also translated into Chinese). He is a regular commentator for Times Higher Education, BBC, and The Conversation on metaverse developments.
variants.bioart:
Professor Andy Miah is a leading scholar and curator of bioart — the intersection of biological science, ethics, and contemporary artistic practice. He edited Human Futures: Art in an Age of Uncertainty (FACT & Liverpool University Press, 2008), one of the defining anthologies of the field, and has written extensively on bioart as a form of bioethical inquiry, examining artists including Stelarc, Orlan, Eduardo Kac, and the Critical Art Ensemble.

He co-organised the International Symposium on Electronic Arts (ISEA) in Belfast (2009), co-chaired the programme theme on Posthumanism, and has collaborated with artists on projects including Project Daedalus (NESTA/AHRC, £125,000, with Abandon Normal Devices and Marshmallow Laser Feast), Alienated Life (NERC public engagement, Chernobyl exclusion zone), and the Evidence Dolls project (with Dunne & Raby, RCA). He has given talks on bioart at the Royal College of Art, Central St Martins, Glasgow School of Art, Otago University, and the Royal Institution of Great Britain.

His work treats bioart not as spectacle but as a mode of ethical inquiry — using creative practice to surface questions about biotechnology, enhancement, posthumanism, and the future of the human body that conventional academic discourse often struggles to articulate.
variants.future-sport:
Professor Andy Miah has spent over 20 years examining the future of sport — investigating how technology, ethics, genetics, digital media, and cultural change are transforming athletic practice, spectatorship, and governance. His work spans gene doping and enhancement ethics, esports and digital sport, Olympic media, wearable technology, virtual reality in sport, and the social media transformation of major events.

His book Sport 2.0: Transforming Sports for Digital Worlds (MIT Press, 2017) is a comprehensive analysis of how digital technology is reshaping sport across all dimensions — from athlete performance and fan experience to broadcasting, governance, and the emergence of esports. His earlier book Genetically Modified Athletes (Routledge, 2004) remains a foundational text on the ethics of biotechnology in sport. He has advised the International Olympic Committee, International Amateur Athletics Federation, World Anti-Doping Agency, and multiple national sports federations, and has keynoted at Sport Accord Convention, Olympism in Action Forum, Global Sports Week, and the International Sport Business Symposium (Rio, 2016).

He holds both scholarly depth and a strong public profile in this area — having appeared on BBC Newsnight, Sky Sports, The Guardian, and Washington Post on topics ranging from gene doping and Oscar Pistorius to the future of esports at the Olympics and the social media transformation of the Games.
variants.creative-industries:
Professor Andy Miah is an interdisciplinary research leader with over two decades of engagement with the creative industries — as researcher, platform builder, policy adviser, and civic connector. He is Principal Investigator on a £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator mobilising over 250 Greater Manchester SMEs into a CreaTech innovation ecosystem with MediaCity and Salford City Council, encompassing gametech, esports, virtual production, immersive technologies, and metaverse applications.

He is Marketing Manchester Ambassador (2026), a member of the DCMS College of Experts (2025–present), and has worked extensively with GMCA, Factory International, Contact Theatre, Abandon Normal Devices, FutureEverything, and the Manchester Science Festival. He is Commission Chair of the World Technology Games (2025–present) and Board Member of the British Esports Federation (2019–present). He facilitated the launch of the Diaspora Innovation Network (2025, with Aviva Studios and Factory International) and led the AHRC BEYOND Conference and Healthy City Design Congress to Manchester.

His research spans all dimensions of the creative economy — from CreaTech and gametech to arts ethics, science communication, and the civic role of cultural institutions — always with a commitment to inclusive innovation and the social responsibility of the creative sector.
variants.teaching-cv:
Professor Andy Miah is an experienced academic teacher and curriculum designer with over 25 years of university teaching across philosophy, bioethics, science communication, digital culture, sport and emerging technologies. He has designed and led courses at undergraduate and postgraduate level across the UK and internationally, with a consistent commitment to innovative pedagogy and interdisciplinary learning.

He co-directs the MSc in Science Communication & Future Media at the University of Salford and contributes teaching across Biomedical Sciences, Wildlife Conservation, and Biotechnology programmes. Previously at the University of the West of Scotland he designed three original courses — Becoming Posthuman, Cyberculture, and Sport & Spectacle — the first of which received external examiner praise for innovative delivery. He held a decade-long Visiting Professorship at the Royal College of Art (MA Design Interactions, 2006–2016) and has taught at UCL, Glasgow School of Art, Edinburgh College of Art, Central St Martins, Oregon State University, and institutions in the USA, Switzerland, and New Zealand.

His teaching is informed by his research in bioethics, AI ethics, science communication, and digital culture, and is consistently grounded in live examples from practice — from drone technology and esports to gene doping and the Olympic Games. He has supervised doctoral candidates at Salford and UWS, examined PhDs at universities including Glasgow, Warwick, Bournemouth, and Plymouth, and held associate teaching positions at the University of Glasgow and University of Abertay.
